title: Statute of Frauds: coverage, writing, and exceptions
shortTitle: Statute of Frauds: coverage, writing, and exceptions
summary: A statutory writing requirement can restrict enforcement of an otherwise formed agreement.
notes: Work through the particular statute: the class of agreement covered, the writing needed, whose signature is required, and any exception or defense issue. The chapter distinguishes unenforceability from absence of a contract and explores waiver and other legal uses of the agreement. Tolosa supplies a particular Texas loan provision, rather than a universal six-category rule. The historical English categories and modern state comparisons illustrate variation. The full later units on satisfaction and exceptions have not yet been assigned.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 371–383. Open assigned page 371.
